title: David Byrne Explains How Forgotten Ideas Come Back to Life
title_cn: David Byrne Explains How Forgotten Ideas Come Back to Life
summary: History is littered with ideas that have been tossed aside, only for them to gain relevance at some later date. Think of Moby-Dick: forgotten in Melville's time, but now regarded as the great American novel. Or the work of economist Hyman Minsky, which became influential a decade after his death, when the 2008 financial crisis made “the Minsky Moment” a mainstream term. These are just a couple of the things we talk about with the legendary musician David Byrne on today's podcast. Byrne's new book, Sleeping Beauties: Why Good Ideas Go Dormant and How They Wake Up, looks to categorize numerous “sleeping beauties” — ideas that were lost but then rediscovered. Besides Melville and Minsky, we also talk about the lost Roman recipe for concrete and we get into Byrne's thoughts on how to write a song and his own experience of having his music rediscovered by a new generation. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Bloomberg Businessweek Daily Podcast: AI Jitters Persist
title_cn: Bloomberg Businessweek Daily Podcast: AI Jitters Persist
summary:
The people, companies and trends shaping the global economy. Watch Carol and Tim LIVE every day on YouTube: http://bit.ly/3vTiACF

Another burst of selling in technology companies rattled Wall Street on Friday, dragging down stocks as investors questioned the outlook for the artificial-intelligence trade. A rout in chipmakers extended into an eighth straight day on worries over whether the buildout of AI infrastructure has outrun the ability of firms to get a return on their investments. Meantime, Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh described AI as potentially the most consequential change to the US and global economy in his lifetime.

On today's episode:
Mike McKee, Bloomberg News International Economics & Policy Correspondent
Max Chafkin, Bloomberg Businessweek Senior Reporter
Patrick McGee, Author of 'Apple in China: The Capture of the World's Greatest Company'
Jason Leopold, Bloomberg News Senior Investigative Reporter (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Warsh Touts ‘Consequential’ AI, Trump Press Secretary Out After Five Days
title_cn: Warsh Touts ‘Consequential’ AI, Trump Press Secretary Out After Five Days
summary: Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh described AI as potentially the most consequential change to the US and global economy in his lifetime, calling it a positive supply shock over the medium term. We get reaction from Bloomberg's Enda Curran. One flagship AI data center in Norway is six months behind schedule, with workers set to be housed in a floating hotel to get it over the finish line. Bloomberg's Brody Ford explains. Katie Zacharia will no longer serve as President Donald Trump’s press secretary after spending less than a week on the job. Bloomberg's Skylar Woodhouse reports from the White House. Veda Partners' Henrietta Treyz examines the road to US midterms. Plus - Bloomberg News US Sports Reporter Randall Williams discusses the NFL's Fall Meeting and the mystery swirling around the next Super Bowl halftime headliner. All on the latest episode of Bloomberg Businessweek Daily. (Source: Bloomberg)
